rituals.name: THE BLAME PIE
rituals.unique_game_move: Imagine A Pie → Check The Whole → Choose Repair
rituals.recognition_cue: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.immediate_need: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.match_reason: Personalisation · Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.goal: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.
rituals.win: ✓ My slice stayed mine; the rest went back to the whole pie.
rituals.winReward: ✓ My slice stayed mine; the rest went back to the whole pie.
rituals.tips:
• Give self-compassion enough time to change the next moment.
• Choose growth first, then decide what self-blame needs.
• Choose self-compassion before deciding what self-blame means.
• Give self-compassion more authority than self-punishment.
• Guilt does not cancel your access to self-respect.

rituals.name: THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST
rituals.unique_game_move: Picture → Name Likely → Select Direction
rituals.recognition_cue: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
rituals.immediate_need: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
rituals.match_reason: Value disconnection · A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
rituals.goal: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture — Picture two arrows.
2. Make Room — One shows the next hour if you obey the thought; the other reveals what unfolds over sixty minutes when you make room for it but follow a chosen value.
3. Name Likely — Name the likely behaviour at each arrow’s end.
4. Select Direction — Select by direction, not by mental volume.
rituals.win: ✓ The room became larger than the mental pull.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The room became larger than the mental pull.
rituals.tips:
• Give loss time to change before choosing value abandonment.
• One dose of what still matters can reopen connection.
• A meaning struggle is real; grief judging is still optional.
• Keep one part of your mind available for purpose.
• Let purpose guide the response, even with the ache of change present.

rituals.name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.ritual_name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.unique_game_move: Close Door → Reopen Choice → Choose Next
rituals.recognition_cue: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.immediate_need: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.match_reason: Decision paralysis · A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.goal: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.steps:
1. Close Door — Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Read Protest — Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Reopen Choice — Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Choose Next — Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.
rituals.win: ✓ Thirty seconds of closure made the real reaction easier to hear.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Thirty seconds of closure made the real reaction easier to hear.
rituals.tips:
• You can honour decision pressure and still refuse deadline pressure.
• One pause can protect room to think from rushing.
• Let control guide you when forced certainty starts sounding convincing.
• Choose a reversible choice before the pressure asks for perfection.
• Make room for urgency without making it the boss.
rituals.supports:
• You can honour decision pressure and still refuse deadline pressure.
• One pause can protect room to think from rushing.
• Let control guide you when forced certainty starts sounding convincing.
• Choose a reversible choice before the pressure asks for perfection.

rituals.ifALittle: Good—decision paralysis moved but did not clear. Tell ThinkStill what is still strongest around bright first line; the next move must target a different mechanism.
rituals.ifNotYet: No forcing it. CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS is a miss for decision paralysis this round. ThinkStill should leave bright first line behind and switch to a different mechanism.

rituals.ritual_name: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
rituals.unique_game_move: Press Equal → Step Down → Reach Zero
rituals.recognition_cue: Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.

rituals.goal: Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.
rituals.steps:
1. Press Equal — Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Match Force — Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Step Down — Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach Zero — Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and observe whether the urge to press returns.

rituals.ritual_name: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
rituals.unique_game_move: No Sentences → Spot The Return → Choose An Exit

rituals.name: IMAGINE THE INNER MACHINE
rituals.unique_game_move: Imagine The Parts → Find One Change Point → Test It
rituals.recognition_cue: Chaos becomes editable after signals and loops are visible.
rituals.immediate_need: Chaos becomes editable after signals and loops are visible.
rituals.match_reason: Impulse fusion · Chaos becomes editable after signals and loops are visible.
rituals.goal: Chaos becomes editable after signals and loops are visible.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine The Parts — Imagine the trigger, meaning, physical feeling, urge, action, result, and feedback.
2. See The Links — Imagine how each part affects the next and where the loop returns.
3. Find the Lever — Notice one place where a small change may shift the whole loop.
4. Test It — Try that small change once.
rituals.win: ✓ One inner-machine dial moved; chaos became editable.
rituals.winReward: ✓ One inner-machine dial moved; chaos became editable.
rituals.tips:
• When the pull to act rises, return to one safer choice.
• Keep your options visible when action pressure gets loud.
• Your choice around an impulse can be simple: a short delay.
• A craving can be loud without earning control of your next move.
• Do not confuse an impulse with a permanent verdict.

rituals.name: THE FRAME CAN WAIT
rituals.challenge: Not knowing how to join a conversation
rituals.primary_trigger: Not knowing how to join a conversation
rituals.unique_game_move: Conversation entry via one-inch frame: Complete one bridge → Rail before noise → Use one mirror → One pocket step → Reframe one bookmark
rituals.recognition_cue: One pocket step is the hinge between this pressure and your ability to make contact before confidence.
rituals.situation: Not knowing how to join a conversation
rituals.immediate_need: One pocket step is the hinge between this pressure and your ability to make contact before confidence.
rituals.match_reason: Conversation entry · One pocket step is the hinge between this pressure and your ability to make contact before confidence.
rituals.goal: One pocket step is the hinge between this pressure and your ability to make contact before confidence.
rituals.steps:
1. Complete one bridge — Make one-inch frame the size of one move through the conversation in front of you; finish the action on one-inch frame, then reassess.
2. Rail before noise — Put one-inch frame around one real question in the conversation in front of you; give one-inch frame one active lane and park each competing demand beyond it.
3. Use one mirror — Make one-inch frame the size of one move through the conversation in front of you; finish the action on one-inch frame, then reassess; Use one mirror is the cue to resume.
4. One pocket step — Use one-inch frame as the doorway view on the conversation in front of you; let one-inch frame describe the scene without defending either side.
5. Reframe one bookmark — Move one-inch frame one pace outside the conversation in front of you; look back from one-inch frame and name what a fair observer would notice first.
rituals.win: ✓ One pocket step changed the ending; you made contact before confidence.
rituals.winReward: ✓ One pocket step changed the ending; you made contact before confidence.

• Start before debate; use another angle.
• Let motion prove itself; widen the frame.

rituals.primary_trigger: Wanting to repair after an argument in the moment
rituals.unique_game_move: Repair hesitation via near signal: Cool the rope → Frame warm doorway → Delay one thread → Tilt one rope → Step back from the second step
rituals.recognition_cue: Shrink the moment to Delay one thread, then make one honest repair.
rituals.situation: Wanting to repair after an argument in the moment
rituals.immediate_need: Shrink the moment to Delay one thread, then make one honest repair.
rituals.match_reason: Repair hesitation · Shrink the moment to Delay one thread, then make one honest repair.
rituals.goal: Shrink the moment to Delay one thread, then make one honest repair.
rituals.steps:
1. Cool the rope — Put near signal between the conversation in front of you and anything irreversible; let near signal guard what a fast reaction could damage.
2. Frame warm doorway — Put near signal around one repair sentence in the conversation in front of you; let near signal close the gate on competing demands until this move ends.
3. Delay one thread — Let near signal protect the next minute from the conversation in front of you; keep near signal between you and any big action until the real cost is clear.
4. Tilt one rope — Move near signal one pace outside the conversation in front of you; look back from near signal and name what a fair observer would notice first.
5. Step back from the second step — Use near signal as the doorway view on the conversation in front of you; let near signal describe the scene without defending either side.
rituals.win: ✓ Near signal did its job: you made one honest repair.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Near signal did its job: you made one honest repair.

• Keep irreversible moves waiting; widen the frame.

rituals.name: ONE SINGLE CONTRACT. THEN MOVE.
rituals.challenge: Nobody is sure who owns the next step in the moment
rituals.primary_trigger: Nobody is sure who owns the next step in the moment
rituals.unique_game_move: Ownership blur via single contract: Guard one brief → Gentle checkpoint first → Gentle frame first → Choose one bridge → Compare the bridge
rituals.recognition_cue: Choose One Bridge and make the next owner impossible to miss.
rituals.situation: Nobody is sure who owns the next step in the moment
rituals.immediate_need: Choose One Bridge and make the next owner impossible to miss.
rituals.match_reason: Ownership blur · Choose One Bridge and make the next owner impossible to miss.
rituals.goal: Choose One Bridge and make the next owner impossible to miss.
rituals.steps:
1. Guard one brief — Let single contract protect the next minute from the team issue; keep single contract between you and any big action until the real cost is clear.
